top.title: Dolphins' rebuild is working despite 1-7 record, and proof is on field
top.description: MIAMI GARDENS ― The Miami Dolphins may be the most optimistic, positive, encouraged 1-7 team in pro sports history and I'm all for it. "Bright future," Dolphins veteran linebacker Jordyn Brooks said after a 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions that put a wrap on the first half of the Dolphins' 18-week NFL schedule. The Dolphins take too many penalties (11 on Sunday), wear down in the second half of games (little depth) and do not score enough red zone touchdowns (none on Sunday). Yet, somehow, nobody is crying, nobody is complaining and nobody is throwing water coolers. I'm all for it. That's because wins and losses were never an important part of evaluating the Dolphins' 2026 season. It's all the other stuff. And so far, all the other stuff has been, well, encouraging. "Right now, I'm angry because I hate to lose," Miami coach Jeff Hafley said , when asked if he is more encouraged than discouraged by the first half of his first NFL season. But then Hafley gave the important part of the answer: "I'm encouraged with this team. I'm encouraged the way they work. I'm encouraged because we've challenged them to play the game a certain way. I'm encouraged because we've asked them to practice a certain way. I'm encouraged because, in my opinion, the Detroit Lions are probably the most physical team in the world. Because in my opinion, the Detroit Lions are probably the most physical team in the NFL. And that's the way they coach and that's the way we play. And I would say we went toe to toe with them." Miami Dolphins rebuild roster set up this 1-7 record If that was bullcrap, I would call it out. It's not. The Dolphins are reaching their 2026 goals as set by ― me. Play hard. Relentless effort. Positive attitude and culture. Player growth and development. It's happening, despite that entirely irrelevant 1-7 record. "Our young guys, man, our rookies, I think that they, they got a bright future, man," said Brooks, the veteran linebacker. "I think Sully (GM Jon-Eric Sullivan) did a great job. Bring these guys in, he brought the right guys in, and not just because they're out there making plays, but just the right guys, right people that you want in the locker room to go through something like this one in seven losing. Losing is not easy, but I think it reveals who you are in that moment." It is a bit discouraging in the first half of the Dolphins' season that quarterback Malik Willis has not yet shown he can definitely be counted on as the 2027 starter. top.title: Trump admits his mass deportation policy was ‘too tough’
top.description: US President Donald Trump said that his mass deportation of undocumented immigrants was “too tough,” according to an excerpt of an interview with CBS aired Sunday. Asked about his deportation policy, Trump told CBS’ “60 Minutes”: “I think it was too tough…I think it might be too tough.” The excerpt was published by CBS on X ahead of a broadcast of the interview on network TV later Sunday. It was recorded after the Republican Party’s heavy loss in midterm elections on Tuesday. While Trump has won some domestic support for securing the US southern border, his administration’s aggressive push to deport millions of undocumented migrants has drawn widespread criticism. However, Trump on Friday appointed the architect of that hardline policy, Stephen Miller, as his chief of staff on Friday, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after the Republican election loss. Miller has been synonymous with scenes of masked immigration agents committing violence after he backed federal agents who shot and killed two Americans early this year. top.title: #23 Men’s Soccer Blanks #25 UCLA 2-0 to Reach the Big Ten Semifinals
top.description: SEATTLE, Wash. — Joshua Jerome had been on the field for 83 seconds when he scored. Matty Lynch had been on for 145. That was all Rutgers needed. The third-seeded Scarlet Knights beat sixth-seeded UCLA 2-0 in the Big Ten Tournament quarterfinals on Sunday afternoon at Husky Soccer Stadium. Rafael Ponce de Leon made five saves for Rutgers’ sixth clean sheet of the season, and it was the program’s first Big Ten Tournament win since they lifted the trophy at Yurcak Field in 2022. Rutgers came west at 8-6-2, 6-3-1 in the Big Ten and No. 23 in the country, back in the conference tournament for the first time since 2023 after finishing third in the league. They closed the regular season with a 4-1 win at No. 8 Michigan State on Oct. 30, when Amer Lukovic scored twice and Ponce de Leon saved a penalty with four minutes left, and on Tuesday the Big Ten named Ponce de Leon its Goalkeeper of the Week. The Scarlet Knights had already beaten UCLA once, 3-1 at Yurcak in the Big Ten opener on Sept. 11, a night when the Bruins scored in the third minute and did not put another shot on target. Sunday’s win was Rutgers’ second over UCLA in 58 days. UCLA arrived 9-3-5 and 4-3-3 in the Big Ten, ranked No. 25, and nearly did not arrive at all. The Bruins started the final day of the regular season seventh on 12 points with six teams qualifying, then beat No. 6 Washington 1-0 on Wednesday when Diego Castano scored from beyond midfield, his team-leading eighth goal of the year, and got the rest of what they needed from Northwestern’s win over Wisconsin. Ryan Jorden’s side were also the defending champions. As a four seed a year ago, UCLA won 2-0 at No. 1 Maryland and beat Michigan 5-0 in the final, and in October 2025 they had beaten Rutgers 5-2 in Westwood. Castano and Jaime Amaro, the Spaniard who transferred in from Bryant and has six goals and five assists this fall, carry the attack. Castano started Sunday on the bench. Ponce de Leon did not have to make a save the last time these teams met. He made five on Sunday. top.title: ‘Worth half a goal’ – Fermin Lopez hails Lamine Yamal’s assist as Barcelona beat Atletico
top.description: Fermin Lopez hailed Lamine Yamal for his excellent pass that set up Barcelona’s winner in a 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid on Sunday night in La Liga. Barcelona went behind in the match but hit back through Lopez. The Spain star then added a second, firing home after a brilliant pass by Yamal. Lopez says Yamal’s contribution was worth “half a goal” as he celebrated a huge win at the top of the table in Spain. “May the connection with Lamine continue, we know each other very well, the pass for the second goal is half a goal, I’m very happy for him too,” he told Movistar. Barcelona looked out of sorts at the start of the match, going behind to Guiliano Simeone’s early goal, and Lopez admitted it was a tough encounter. “It was a very difficult match, last year they beat us in the Cup and Champions League, we knew what they were going to propose to us, but we knew how to come back from the game,” he explained. “We weren’t sharp, but with the goal we freed ourselves, played our game and won.” Victory sees Barcelona move five points clear of Atletico in the table, with Simeone’s men dropping to third after their defeat.

top.description: Why Arsenal’s Full-Backs Are Crucial To Arteta’s Tactical System – Opinion One of the most interesting aspects of Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal is the way his team uses its full-backs. Traditionally, full-backs were expected to provide width, overlap with wingers and deliver crosses into the penalty area. Under Arteta, however, their responsibilities have become far more complex. Rather than simply staying out wide, Arsenal’s full-backs frequently move into central areas of the pitch, helping the team dominate possession and control midfield. This tactical approach, commonly known as using inverted full-backs, has become an important part of Arsenal’s identity, as Dan Smith explored in Arteta’s tactical evolution . Creating Numerical Advantages And Controlling Possession The main purpose of inverting a full-back is to create an additional passing option in midfield. When Arsenal build from the back, one of their full-backs can move inside alongside the central midfielders, giving the team an extra player in the middle of the pitch. This makes it considerably more difficult for opponents to press Arsenal effectively. If an opposition midfielder follows the full-back into the centre, space can open up elsewhere. If they remain in position, Arsenal gain a numerical advantage. This is particularly important against opponents who defend with a compact shape. Rather than relying entirely on their centre-backs and midfielders to progress possession, Arsenal can create new passing angles and move the opposition’s defensive structure around. The result is a team that can patiently build attacks while maintaining control of central areas. (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images) Defensive Security And The Importance Of Player Profiles When Arsenal commit players forward, they inevitably leave spaces that opponents will look to exploit. Having a full-back positioned centrally can help reduce this risk. Instead of being caught too far up the pitch, the inverted full-back provides additional protection in front of the centre-backs, allowing Arsenal to maintain a stronger defensive structure when possession is lost. It also helps the team react quickly to transitions, attempting to win the ball back before the opposition can launch a dangerous counterattack. Of course, this approach is not without its risks. If opponents successfully bypass Arsenal’s initial pressure, the spaces left in wide areas can become vulnerable. Inverting also requires a different skill set from traditional wide defending. Players must be comfortable receiving the ball under pressure, making quick decisions and operating in congested midfield areas. They also need the positional awareness to understand when to move inside and when to provide width. top.title: Mohsin Naqvi's PCB backs Mike Hesson to continue as Pakistan's Test coach
top.description: Pakistan's white-ball head coach Mike Hesson will continue to look after the country's Test team as interim head coach until the end of the current World Test Championship (WTC) cycle. Hesson took charge of the red-ball side during Pakistan's difficult tour of England two months ago, after former coach Sarfaraz Ahmed was removed midway through the series. A source in the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) confirmed it to Indian news agency PTI that Hesson had agreed to continue in the role and would also guide the team during next year's Test series against New Zealand. "Hesson will also be interim head coach for next year's Test series against New Zealand. The board and head coach have both conveyed this to the players as well," the source said. Hesson's future with Pakistan cricket Hesson joined Pakistan as white-ball head coach in May 2025 before taking temporary charge of the Test team. However, his long-term future with the PCB will be reviewed after next year's World Cup, which will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. "Hesson's association with Pakistan cricket will be reviewed after next year's World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. It will also then be decided who will be the head coach of the Test side for the next cycle of the World Test Championship," the source added. Questions over Hesson's influence Hesson has become a controversial figure in Pakistan cricket, with several former players and experts questioning the amount of authority he has been given by the PCB, particularly in team selection and other cricketing decisions. Pakistan Test captain Babar Azam also recently admitted that he does not have a say in selection matters. He said his responsibility is to make the best use of the 15-16 players selected by the team management and selection committee. The PCB source also acknowledged that chairman Mohsin Naqvi has great faith in Hesson and trusts him with important cricketing decisions. However, Hesson's frequent changes to the team and players across formats have not gone down well with everyone in Pakistan cricket.

However, Trump on Friday appointed the architect of that hardline policy, Stephen Miller, as his chief of staff on Friday, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after the Republican election loss. nigeria.title: Sultan directs Muslims to sight Jumada Assaniya moon Monday
nigeria.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO – The Sultanate Council of Sokoto has called on Muslims across Nigeria to search for the new crescent moon of Jumada Assaniya 1448AH on Monday, November 9, 2026. The directive was contained in a statement dated November 8, 2026, signed by Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu and made available to journalists on Sunday. According to the statement, the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council identified Monday as the 29th day of Jumada al-Ula 1448AH and the appropriate date for the nationwide moon-sighting exercise. The council urged Muslims across the country to actively participate in the exercise by looking out for the new crescent moon after sunset on Monday. It specifically requested anyone who sights the crescent to promptly report the observation to the nearest District or Village Head for onward transmission to His Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, CFR, mni, the Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA). The council stressed the importance of timely and credible reports of confirmed sightings to enable the Sultan to make the appropriate religious announcement on the commencement of the new Islamic month. It noted that the Sultan remains the recognised authority responsible for communicating the outcome of the moon-sighting exercise to Muslims across the country. The announcement underscores the role of the Sultanate Council in coordinating Islamic religious affairs and guiding the Muslim Ummah on matters concerning the Islamic lunar calendar. In a prayer, Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu, Waziri and Chairman of the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council, asked Allah (SWT) to grant Muslims the guidance and strength to discharge the religious responsibility successfully. nigeria.title: Fermin brace earns Liga leaders Barcelona 2-1 win at Atletico
nigeria.description: Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 and move three points clear at the top of La Liga. The Spanish champions lead second place Real Madrid, who beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, with Atletico third, now five points behind. Giuliano Simeone fired Atletico ahead in a high-octane start, before Lopez pulled Barca level shortly before the interval at the Metropolitano stadium. The 23-year-old Spain international netted the winner after 66 minutes when Lamine Yamal slipped him in. The match started at a fast pace and both teams hit the woodwork in the opening stages. Alvarez, who tried and failed to force a move from Atletico to Barca in the summer, rounded goalkeeper Joan Garcia but could not finish off the chance as the defence blocked his route to goal. From the resulting corner Atletico defender Marc Pubill headed against the crossbar with Garcia beaten. At the other end Pedri crashed a strike against the woodwork after being fed by Barca’s teenage star Lamine Yamal. Atletico took the lead in the 10th minute, slicing Barca’s defence open. Alvarez crossed for Giuliano Simeone to turn home from close range. The game settled down after that pulsating start, although Alvarez came close to scoring Atletico’s second. The Argentine international’s shot was fumbled by Garcia, but the goalkeeper was able to collect the ball quickly afterwards. Yamal blasted into the side-netting from a tight angle with Barcelona not able to click into their top gears. Despite their struggles they went in level at the break, with a goal out of nowhere. Lopez’s path to the box was blocked but the ball bounced loose to the midfielder and he quickly smashed a strike past Jan Oblak. Early in the second half Alvarez lobbed over the crossbar when running in on goal. The forward came to rue the miss when Barcelona took the lead. Yamal played a clever pass through Atletico’s defence and Lopez kept his cool to beat Oblak. It was his seventh league goal in 11 top flight appearances this season. Barcelona kept Atletico at bay well in the final stages to take three points home from the capital before the international break. Earlier on fourth-place Real Betis earned a 2-0 win at Elche, while Real Sociedad, fifth, defeated Rayo Vallecano 1-0. Hamzat, the incumbent Deputy Governor, also disclosed plans to expand water transportation with 77 electric ferries and improve connectivity between different parts of Lagos through an integrated transport system. ﻿ He made the promises on Sunday during the Lagos governorship debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, The Cable, and Vanguard Newspaper. Explaining his transportation plans, Hamzat said the objective was to reduce commuting time and give residents more opportunities to rest and spend time with their families. “The plan is to give back time to the citizens to plan, to rest, to spend with their family. There’s nowhere in Africa that the private sector has funded a rail. “Since BRT started, it has done 77 million journeys; that is with 1,000 buses. My plan says we will push it to 4,000 buses; the idea is to move one million people a day with 4,000 CNG buses, meaning up to 5,000, create BRt lane from Marina to Epe, from Marina to Badagry and so on and so forth,” he said. “Today, over four million people have the Cowry card. What does that mean? It means you can use ferry, you can use rail, and you can use BRT buses — one payment — so that we can deal with how to subsidise it. On healthcare, the APC candidate promised to expand access to medical services by increasing the number of primary healthcare centres providing round-the-clock services. nigeria.title: Seven killed, over 100 injured in Egypt train collision
nigeria.description: At least seven people have been killed and more than 100 injured after two trains collided near Giza, Egypt, causing several carriages to derail and plunge down an embankment. The country’s railway authority said the trains, travelling south from Giza and Cairo, collided in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat. Egypt’s President, Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, said he had directed relevant authorities to investigate the circumstances surrounding the accident and ensure that anyone found negligent was held accountable. The public prosecutor’s office warned that the death toll could rise as rescue and recovery operations continued. The government said hospitals in the affected area had been placed on heightened alert to handle the large number of casualties. Health Minister, Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, said victims were receiving treatment for various injuries, including broken bones and head injuries. The Egyptian Red Crescent also deployed personnel to provide emergency assistance and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene. The ministry confirmed that the driver of one of the trains was among those killed in the collision. According to reports, the first train was travelling from Giza to Fayoum when it crashed into the rear of another train heading from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks. Photographs from the scene showed several overturned carriages, with emergency responders and members of the public searching through the wreckage for survivors. Train services between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were deployed to remove the damaged trains. The railway authority had yet to announce when services would resume. The crash occurred close to the location of Egypt’s deadliest railway disaster, which happened in February 2002 when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor, killing more than 370 people officially, although some estimates put the death toll higher. Two other train accidents in the area in 2009 also claimed dozens of lives. The latest disaster sparked calls on Sunday for Egypt’s transport minister to resign over the recurring railway accidents. Meanwhile, foreign governments and diplomatic representatives expressed condolences and solidarity with Egypt over the tragedy. Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed solidarity with Egypt and wished the injured a speedy recovery. Turkey’s Ambassador to Egypt also conveyed his condolences on X to the victims, their families and the Egyptian people. nigeria.title: No Political Will To Deal With Agberos In Lagos, Says NDC’s Funsho Doherty
nigeria.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Lagos State, Funsho Doherty, has blamed the persistence of the agbero system in the state on a lack of political will by successive administrations to reform the transport sector. Agberos are transport touts who collect money from commercial bus drivers and other transport operators at motor parks, bus stops and along roads, often claiming to represent transport unions or park authorities. Speaking during the Lagos Governorship Debate on Sunday, Doherty said powerful interests within the existing transport system had made it difficult for successive governments to tackle the activities of the operators. The debate was organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, a coalition of five media organisations: Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard Newspapers. “Many of us understand this notion of the agbero system that people talk about. There is no political will to deal with that problem,” Doherty said. He argued that meaningful reform of public transportation would require a government that was accountable to residents rather than interests benefiting from the existing arrangement. “We will modernise the transportation system because we will be elected by the people, not by an agbero network,” he said. nigeria.title: Police rescue five kidnap victims, arrest three suspects in Kebbi
nigeria.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has rescued five kidnapped victims and arrested three suspects following a coordinated security operation in Dakingari, Suru Local Government Area of the state. The victims were identified as Samaila Abubakar, 35; Dayyaba Muhammadu, 32; and Balki Hakimi, 31. According to the statement, police operatives, working in collaboration with local vigilantes, swiftly mobilised to the area and pursued the assailants. Makinde stated this on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, where he outlined his proposed security reforms ahead of the party’s presidential campaign activities in the city. “I believe that we need to decentralise our security architecture. State police is one of the ways to achieve this, but it must be properly structured. “States that are ready should be allowed to establish their own police formations, while others can come on board when they are prepared,” he said. Recalling his engagement with former President Muhammadu Buhari on the issue in 2019, Makinde said the former president had expressed concerns about the ability of some states to fund their police formations. “When we approached President Buhari in 2019, one of the concerns he raised was that some states could not even pay workers’ salaries. He questioned how such states would be able to fund state police,” he said. Explaining the alternative adopted by governors in the South-West, Makinde said they settled for a regional security arrangement through Amotekun. He said the operatives gather intelligence and work with federal security agencies, adding that the initiative had helped improve security coordination in the region. Some people are worried that governors could use state police to oppress their opponents or intimidate citizens. Those concerns are valid, and we must put safeguards in place. “But the fact that something can be abused does not mean we should not do it. We must design a system that ensures accountability and protects the rights of the people,” he said. On the pace of implementation, Makinde said states should be allowed to establish their police formations at different times, depending on their readiness and capacity. nigeria.title: ‘That’s not going to happen’ – Carrick rules out resigning as Man United boss
nigeria.description: Michael Carrick said he expects to “move forward and keep working” as Manchester United manager despite dropping into the Premier League relegation zone. United twice came from two goals down to salvage a remarkable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday. Goals in stoppage time from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point and potentially gave Carrick a stay of execution ahead of a two-week international break. “We haven’t won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on the things that we’ve been working on,” Carrick told Sky Sports. “Showing a lot of the good (things) in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.” Results this weekend dropped United into the bottom three after August for the first time in 40 years. “We’re in November,” added Carrick. “I don’t like the situation where we are, I don’t like the results that we’ve had, but we can definitely do something about it.” The former United midfielder dismissed any suggestion he could resign if it was in the best interests of the club and said he would not seek out discussions with his superiors on where his future lies. “That’s not going to happen,” said Carrick when asked if he would resign. “I’m quite clear what direction the club needs to go in, and we’ve just got to win games.” The 45-year-old added: “I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there… as a normal international week is, we’ll have some training, we’ll have one or two days off, not too much, but we’ll train and get ready for the next game.” United travel to rivals Liverpool when they are next in action on November 22. nigeria.title: 2027: Nigeria needs reset, not reforms — Makinde
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has said Nigeria needs a fundamental reset rather than mere reforms to address its economic, security and governance challenges ahead of the 2027 general elections. Makinde spoke on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, ahead of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off scheduled for Monday in the city. Explaining his position, the governor argued that reforms were insufficient where the problems in a system outweighed its strengths. “When you talk about reform, it means that there is something good in the system that you want to improve upon. But when the bad outweighs the good, you need to take a different course of action. “If what you have in the system is only about 20 per cent of what you expected, you don’t need to continue tweaking it. You need to press the reset button, shut it down and reboot it. That is what Nigeria needs at this point. Reform will not work in the present environment,” he said. The governor said he did not initially intend to become a politician but was motivated by concerns about the country’s future. “I am not a career politician. I came into politics because I believe that the future of millions of Nigerians is at stake. We have the potential to become the greatest Black nation on the face of the earth, but we must make the right decisions to achieve that destiny,” he said. On the economy, Makinde identified it as the foremost priority of his proposed Reset Agenda, arguing that economic performance should be measured by improvements in the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians. “The economy must work for everybody. We should not just be talking about foreign reserves, World Bank figures or inflation statistics. What matters is whether ordinary Nigerians can afford to feed themselves and meet their basic needs,” he said. He added that economic progress should be assessed by its impact on households rather than statistical indicators alone. “If the people on the streets are not feeling any improvement, then we cannot say that the economy is doing well. nigeria.title: Customs processes 99,839 cargo declarations in two months
nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) processed 9,195 Pre-Arrival Assessment Reports (PAARs) and 99,839 Single Goods Declarations (SGDs) between September and October 2026, generating a combined revenue of approximately ₦1.42 trillion. The figures were disclosed during a joint security press briefing at the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), under the Office of the National Security Adviser, in Abuja. Speaking at the briefing, the National Public Relations Officer of the NCS, Deputy Comptroller Abdullahi Aliyu Maiwada, said the performance reflected the Service’s commitment to facilitating legitimate trade, improving cargo clearance and strengthening revenue generation through digital interventions and collaboration with stakeholders. A breakdown of the figures showed that the Service processed 2,102 PAARs in September and 7,093 in October, bringing the total to 9,195. Similarly, 48,832 SGDs were processed in September, while 51,007 were recorded in October, giving a combined total of 99,839 declarations. The Service collected ₦697.8 billion in revenue in September and ₦722.9 billion in October, amounting to ₦1.4207 trillion during the two-month period. In a statement, Maiwada also disclosed that the Service recorded significant progress in export trade facilitation. At the Lilypond Export Command, export activities in the third quarter of 2026 generated a total export value of $752.85 million, compared with $586.15 million recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The statement put the increase at approximately 28.44 per cent, reflecting the growing contribution of the export sector and the impact of measures aimed at facilitating non-oil exports. On enforcement, the NCS said it seized prohibited and restricted items with a combined Duty Paid Value exceeding ₦8.1 billion during the period under review. The interceptions covered various categories, including illicit drugs, pharmaceutical products, prohibited goods and petroleum products. The Service said it continued to collaborate with relevant regulatory and security agencies to ensure the appropriate handling and disposition of seized items. On its anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) responsibilities, the NCS highlighted the ongoing World Customs Organisation (WCO) Mentoring Mission, inaugurated on October 19, 2026. The four-week engagement, scheduled to run from October 18 to November 13, 2026, is designed to strengthen the capacity of the Service to identify, investigate and tackle trade-based money laundering and other illicit financial activities associated with cross-border trade. nigeria.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Funso Doherty, has said the private sector cannot independently address the state’s housing crisis, urging the government to take a leading role in providing affordable accommodation. Doherty made the remarks during the Lagos governorship debate held in Lagos on Sunday and organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.title: Why Arsenal’s Full-Backs Are Crucial To Arteta’s Tactical System – Opinion
sports.description: Why Arsenal’s Full-Backs Are Crucial To Arteta’s Tactical System – Opinion One of the most interesting aspects of Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal is the way his team uses its full-backs. Traditionally, full-backs were expected to provide width, overlap with wingers and deliver crosses into the penalty area. Under Arteta, however, their responsibilities have become far more complex. Rather than simply staying out wide, Arsenal’s full-backs frequently move into central areas of the pitch, helping the team dominate possession and control midfield. This tactical approach, commonly known as using inverted full-backs, has become an important part of Arsenal’s identity, as Dan Smith explored in Arteta’s tactical evolution . Creating Numerical Advantages And Controlling Possession The main purpose of inverting a full-back is to create an additional passing option in midfield. When Arsenal build from the back, one of their full-backs can move inside alongside the central midfielders, giving the team an extra player in the middle of the pitch. This makes it considerably more difficult for opponents to press Arsenal effectively. If an opposition midfielder follows the full-back into the centre, space can open up elsewhere. If they remain in position, Arsenal gain a numerical advantage. This is particularly important against opponents who defend with a compact shape. Rather than relying entirely on their centre-backs and midfielders to progress possession, Arsenal can create new passing angles and move the opposition’s defensive structure around. The result is a team that can patiently build attacks while maintaining control of central areas. (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images) Defensive Security And The Importance Of Player Profiles When Arsenal commit players forward, they inevitably leave spaces that opponents will look to exploit. Having a full-back positioned centrally can help reduce this risk. Instead of being caught too far up the pitch, the inverted full-back provides additional protection in front of the centre-backs, allowing Arsenal to maintain a stronger defensive structure when possession is lost. It also helps the team react quickly to transitions, attempting to win the ball back before the opposition can launch a dangerous counterattack. Of course, this approach is not without its risks. Pakistan Test captain Babar Azam also recently admitted that he does not have a say in selection matters. He said his responsibility is to make the best use of the 15-16 players selected by the team management and selection committee. science.title: Legendary sci-fi magazine 'Starlog' returns as a yearly release, just in time for its 50th anniversary
science.description: null "Starlog" was one of the greatest sci-fi and fantasy magazines ever, and after a 17-year absence, it's being resurrected. The legendary sci-fi mag went dark back in 2009 as part of the wave of popular publications folding due to years of declining readership and subscriptions. But as of Nov. 13, this geek favorite periodical returns as an annual print edition, and it's available for pre-order now. It’s another indication of digital fatigue in the world, and fans of a certain age will recall the pleasure of poring over each colorful issue packed with in-depth interviews, behind-the-scenes photos, TV guides, classic movie retrospectives, book reviews, con news, and VFX features. The triumphant relaunch of "Starlog" magazine happens on Nov. 13, 2026 (Image credit: Fangoria Holdings) "Starlog" launched in 1976, in the pre-" Star Wars " days, under the leadership of editor-in-chief Terry O’Quinn. It first arrived with artist Jack Thurston's beautiful painted "Star Trek" cover, featuring William Shatner as Captain James T. Kirk and Leonard Nimoy’s Spock, set against the U.S.S. Enterprise near a shimmering black hole. The magazine continued to inform the science fiction community about upcoming sci-fi TV shows and blockbuster Hollywood films for over three decades; I fondly recall reading each informative and entertaining monthly issue cover-to-cover. Just in time to honor its 50th anniversary this year, "Starlog" blasts back into the sci-fi universe with Issue #375 showcasing cover artwork created by Armenian artist Gabriel Yeganyan. Its geek culture legacy, covering iconic franchises like "Star Wars," "Star Trek," and "Alien," will now live on thanks to Fangoria Holdings and io9 co-founder Annalee Newitz, editor-in-chief. Three vintage "Starlog" magazine issues from my personal collection! (Image credit: Jeff Spry) "During its original 33-year run, 'Starlog' documented science fiction as it evolved across film, television, books, technology, and culture," said 'Fangoria's Tara Ansley. "Fifty years after the magazine first launched, the line between science fiction and the real world has become increasingly difficult to separate. That makes this an especially interesting time to bring 'Starlog' back. Technology may change, but the most compelling questions have always been about people: how we live, what we create, and what kind of future we want to build." "Starlog" reloads for its first annual edition after a long hiatus on Nov. 13. You can pre-order the first issue (Issue 375 in continuity) on the Starlog website .

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
science.description: null On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this. It performed well, but eventually it stopped listening to commands. The spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere in January 2015. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the Venus Express spacecraft to Venus on Nov. 8, 2005.. (Image credit: ESA) Why it mattered Venus Express established ESA as the third world organization to successfully send a probe to study Venus, following the United States and Soviet Union. (Japan's JAXA became the fourth five years later.) "By studying Venus, scientists learn how Earth-like planets change over time," reads a summary of the planet's exploration prepared by The Planetary Society. "Orbital studies [like Venus Express] hint that Venus may have hosted habitable oceans before becoming inhospitable." "By studying Venus, we can learn how Earth-like planets evolve and what shapes planets throughout the galaxy into temperate, lush worlds instead of sweltering hothouses. Venus also helps scientists model Earth’s climate, and may serve as a cautionary tale on how dramatically a planet’s climate can change," wrote the Society. An illustration of the Venus Express spacecraft in orbit around Venus. (Image credit: ESA) ESA returned to Venus in 2018 when BepiColombo, its joint mission with JAXA, used the planet's gravity to redirect its path toward the planet Mercury. Want more space history? Though the three-headed golden Kaiju might seem like a natural native of Monster Island, King Ghidorah actually emerged from the depths of space. However, it isn't just the origins of King Ghidorah — also known as Monster Zero in the Godzilla movie Invasion of Astro-Monster (1965) — that are this beast's only cosmic connection. One of the largest structures in the universe, the King Ghidorah Supercluster , was named in honor of Godzilla's primary antagonist. Eat that, King Kong! King Ghidorah and Godzilla The three heads of King Ghidorah seen in Godzilla Minus Zero (Image credit: Toho Studios) King Ghidorah is a three-headed, twin-tailed golden dragon from the stars, first introduced in the fifth Godzilla movie, Ghidorah, the Three-Headed Monster (1964). In this first appearance, part of the Shōwa era (1964–1975) of Godzilla history, Ghidorah ravaged Venus , wiping out its population 5,000 years before arriving on Earth encased within a highly magnetic meteorite . Ghidorah was bested this first time by Godzilla, Rodan, and Mothra. Undeterred, Ghidorah returned for a rematch just a year later in Invasion of Astro Monster (1965), after being discovered supposedly terrorizing the inhabitants of Planet X, a world found beyond Jupiter . science.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
science.description: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life. To aid in distinguishing between habitable and inhabited planets, planetary scientist Samantha Gilbert-Janizek of the University of California, Riverside, developed a model that simulates the evolution of a rocky planet without life. "The model can help us see how habitable but non-living planets might mimic living planets," Gilbert-Janizek, who was a PhD student at the University of Washington when the research was conducted, said in a statement. Gilbert-Janizek built upon a model previously developed by Washington’s Rory Barnes that simulated the core, mantle, and crust of a planet. This new model pushed the simulation two steps further by incorporating the surface and atmosphere of the planet as well. In all, the model simulates 19 properties of a rocky planet that are not related to life, including the amount of heat a planet receives from its star , the exchange of heat and chemicals from the core to the surface, and the outflow of certain gases from the subsurface. Gilbert-Janizek’s starting point was to simulate the development of Earth had life never arisen here, therefore providing a baseline with which to compare to exoplanets . She ran the simulation from the birth of Earth 4.5 billion years ago to 500 million years into the future. The result was a lifeless world, but one that still had oceans and an atmosphere. "When we interpret observations of an exoplanet’s atmosphere, this tool will help us determine the probability that what we observe indicates life on the surface," said Gilbert-Janizek. An illustration shows the landscape of a primordial Earth before life arose as lightning splits the skies (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) What makes the simulation especially useful is its plug-and-play nature. Researchers can simply apply the bulk properties of whichever planet they are studying to the model, and then just let it run. If the result is a planet with an atmosphere that matches what is detected spectroscopically by the James Webb Space Telescope or, in the future, the various extremely large 30-meter-plus ground-based telescopes or NASA’s planned Habitable Worlds Observatory , then we know that planet probably does not have life as we know it. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. science.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
science.description: null NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. But the road from Artemis II's success to crewed lunar landings and, later, a permanent moon base will take a lot of launches of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket, Isaacman stressed. "You know, a lot of people, especially in the space community, start getting [into] if the landers are there or not. I don't really care about that right now. What I care about is that we are launching big rockets no less than once a year," he said. "I think that's imperative for NASA to be doing these deep-space human spaceflight missions right now," Isaacman added. "So, we had a great mission in April of '26. We will launch again in '27." That coming launch will be for Artemis III, a crewed mission to low Earth orbit that will test docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's private lunar landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. "We need to continue to exercise those muscles," he said, referring to SLS liftoffs. "And, honestly, once a year isn't great, either. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. (Image credit: SpaceX) That touchdown occurred aboard the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange in the Pacific Ocean. It wrapped up the eighth flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1095. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, continued carrying its mystery payload skyward. It could be headed to low Earth orbit , outside observers speculate. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a similar system designed to provide services to the U.S. military and its allies. Starshield satellites are believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so.
